paper.title: Minimax Last-Iterate Convergence in Matrix Games with Observed Actions

settings.name_in_paper: Unknown two-player zero-sum matrix game with bandit payoff feedback and observed opponent actions
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in games with an equilibrium (Nash / duality gap) objective; two coupled learners rather than a single bandit learner.
unmapped: two-player zero-sum matrix game with unknown payoff matrix A in [-1,1]^{d x d}, d actions per player
both players observe the sampled action pair (I_t, J_t) and a common noisy payoff R_t in [-1,1]
objective is last-iterate duality gap Gap(x_t,y_t) of the played mixed strategies, uniformly over all rounds
settings.definition_quote: We consider a two-player zero-sum game with a fixed unknown matrix $A\in[-1,1]^{d\times d}$ ... Conditionally on $\mathcal F_{t-1}$, they independently sample $I_t\sim x_t$ and $J_t\sim y_t$. Both players then observe the action pair $(I_t,J_t)$ and a common payoff $R_t\in[-1,1]$ satisfying $\mathbb E[R_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},I_t,J_t]=A_{I_tJ_t}$.

algorithms.name: Phased exponential weights with ratio correction

conditions: payoffs R_t in [-1,1] with conditional mean A_{I_t J_t}
tuning: confidence delta in (0,1) given as input
phase parameters tau_0 = max{6d, ceil(16384 d H^2/e^2)}, eta = 16H/(e tau_0), e_k = 2^{1-k}, rho_k = delta/2^{k+1}

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: Fix $d\ge2$, $A\in[-1,1]^{d\times d}$, and $\delta\in(0,1)$. Under the feedback model in Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the played strategies of Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} satisfy, simultaneously for all $t\ge1$, \[ \operatorname{Gap}(x_t,y_t) \le C\sqrt{\frac dt} \left[\log\!\left(\frac{dt}{\delta}\right)\right]^{3/2}, \] where $C>0$ is a universal constant.

results.notes: Quantity is the last-iterate duality gap of played strategies (not regret). Equivalently O~(d/eps^2) rounds to reach and keep gap eps. O(d) time and memory per round.
